_readme: InoxTv ads config — ONE file, both apps, both ad networks, on the GMA Next-Gen SDK.
Host at: https://jitendrasoftwaredeveloper.github.io/inoxtv-config/inoxtv-ads.json
READ BY APP 1.1.0 AND LATER. App 1.0.9 in the field reads the OLD file (inoxtv-admob.json)
and cannot see this one. The old file must stay published exactly as it is so 1.0.9 keeps
serving; nothing here can change what a 1.0.9 install does.
Consequence to accept knowingly: until 1.0.9 is retired, an AdMob unit change that must
reach BOTH versions has to be made in both files. Changes that only matter going forward go
here only.
preroll.json is a DIFFERENT file and belongs to the IMA / VAST / VMAP live-TV path. Nothing in
this file touches it, reads it, or can affect an IMA ad.
THE ONE IDEA — every slot has TWO ad sources, adx (Google Ad Manager) and admob, and the
top-level priority list decides which is asked first:
priority: [adx, admob]  = Ad Manager first, AdMob catches anything Ad Manager cannot fill
A source that is switched off, absent, or has no unit for that slot is skipped and the next
source in the list is asked. Reorder this one list to change priority across the whole app —
no other edit, no app release. A list holding one source serves that source only, with no
fallback at all.
FALLBACK HAPPENS AT REQUEST TIME, NOT ONLY AT CONFIG TIME: the app asks the first source's unit
and, when that request fails or comes back with no fill, asks the next source's unit for the
same placement. The SDK caps preloaded ads at 6 app-wide across every format and preload ID,
so on a preloaded format (rewarded, interstitial, app open) the fallback may be a request made
at that moment rather than a standing second preload — a little slower than the first source
would have been, and never a blank screen. Banners fall back the same way.
SWITCHES, widest first — each one is a single edit, no app release:
1. master_enabled ........................ false = no ad anywhere, both networks, both apps
2. sources.<adx|admob>.master_enabled .... false = that one NETWORK goes silent everywhere,
and the other network keeps serving through the priority list
3. <platform>.master_enabled ............. false = that one APP goes silent, the other keeps
running. mobile and tv are independent in every respect.
4. debug_ads_enabled / allow_test_units_in_release, at the global, per-source and per-app
level. Wherever one of these keys is present it must be true as well, so a single stray
true cannot change one network on its own. A debug key can only ever REMOVE test ads from a
debug build; a test-in-release key is the one switch whose wrong value earns nothing while
every ad still looks perfect — see the recipes further down.
5. <platform>.slots.<key>.enabled ........ false = that one placement goes silent everywhere
6. <platform>.slots.<key>.<src>.enabled .. false = that placement is not served by that one
network; the other source still serves it
A slot key the app asks for but this file does not contain behaves exactly like enabled:false.
An unknown source name inside a slot is ignored. Unknown keys anywhere are ignored, so this
file can gain keys later without breaking an app already installed in the field.
WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY READS. Everything else here is documentation for whoever edits the file:
top level ..... master_enabled, debug_ads_enabled, allow_test_units_in_release, priority,
sources, mobile, tv
sources.<src> . master_enabled, debug_ads_enabled, allow_test_units_in_release
per platform .. master_enabled, debug_ads_enabled, reward_gates, reward_unlock_hours, slots
per slot ...... enabled, min_interval_s (app_open only), max_per_session (interstitial only),
adx.enabled, adx.live, adx.test, admob.enabled, admob.live, admob.test
NOT read ...... version, updated, publisher, mobile_app_id, tv_app_id, name, format, phase,
console_refresh_s, _note, _readme
console_refresh_s is the value set on the ad unit in the network's console, recorded here so
this one file tells the whole story. The app cannot change a banner's refresh rate, so
editing that number here changes nothing — change it on the unit in the console.
EVERY DEFAULT IS THE QUIET ONE. A missing or misspelled enabled reads as false, a missing
max_per_session reads as 0 = never, a missing master_enabled reads as false. A file that
loses a key goes silent, never loud. A missing priority list falls back to adx then admob; an
empty one serves the first source only. The one deliberate exception is reward_gates: an empty
or missing value means NO gate is active, because a broken config must never lock a user out
of a feature. Ads fail towards showing less; gates fail towards giving more.
AN EMPTY OR MISSING live IS NOT A KILL SWITCH — it means that source has no unit for that slot,
so the next source in the priority list is asked instead. That is the per-slot rollout lever: a
slot whose adx.live is cleared is served by AdMob alone, with no other edit and no release.
Every adx.live below is filled with this network's real path, so Ad Manager is asked first
everywhere it has a unit; clearing one field hands that one placement back to AdMob, and
clearing all of them returns the app to exactly what 1.0.9 serves today. To silence a
placement for certain, use enabled:false.
TEST vs LIVE — keep BOTH, never overwrite one with the other:
test = the network's demo unit. AdMob: ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/... . Ad Manager:
/21775744923/example/... . Both always fill, neither touches your account, both are safe to
click — which is exactly why they are the only units a debug build may ever request.
live = your real unit. AdMob: ca-app-pub-6161953663322185/<unit>. Ad Manager:
/22853635592/Inoxtv-app-Ad-Units/<unitName> — the ad unit's full path in Ad Manager: network
22853635592, ad unit tree Inoxtv-app-Ad-Units, and that slot's name as the leaf.
Overwriting test with live means a debug build can never show an ad again, and the next 4 dp
banner tweak would need a release build to verify.
debug_ads_enabled and allow_test_units_in_release — GLOBAL *AND* PER NETWORK, and every level
that is present must be true. A stray true on one source therefore cannot change that network
on its own, and the global key stays a real master switch. The recipes:
both networks in test mode ....... allow_test_units_in_release: true; the source keys left
alone
Ad Manager only in test mode ..... global allow_test_units_in_release: true,
sources.adx.allow_test_units_in_release: true,
sources.admob.allow_test_units_in_release: false
one network, debug build ......... sources.<src>.debug_ads_enabled: false
one app, debug build ............. <platform>.debug_ads_enabled: false
The per-network test key is what lets a release-path check — the R8 / minified-APK pass — point
ONE network at its demo units while the other keeps earning. Its risk is real and worth naming:
it is the one value in this file whose wrong setting earns NOTHING while every ad still displays
perfectly. A true left behind is invisible on screen and expensive in production, so set it back
to false the moment the check is done.
The debug keys are safe by construction: they can only REMOVE test ads from a debug build, never
make a debug build request a production unit. Ads never fall through to live in a debug build
either — those would be self-made impressions on your own account, which the networks treat as
invalid traffic. An empty test unit therefore means that source is SKIPPED in debug, the
debug-side twin of an empty live in release.
What that adds up to today: mobile debug serves test ads from BOTH networks — Ad Manager's demo
network first, AdMob's demo unit behind it in the priority list. tv debug still serves nothing
at all, because tv.debug_ads_enabled is false; its test units are filled in below, so flipping
that one key is all it takes to exercise them. No debug build can request a live unit from
either network, on either app.
AD MANAGER UNITS — network 22853635592, ad unit tree Inoxtv-app-Ad-Units:
A GAM ad unit is a PATH, /<networkCode>/<unitName>. It is not a ca-app-pub-... ID and it
belongs to no AdMob unit. Every adx.live below is that network and that tree plus the slot's
own name, so the path here and the unit in the console stay in step by construction.
Every slot needs its OWN GAM unit, created with the MATCHING format. A path carries no format,
so a banner unit pasted into unlock_rew returns no fill and raises no error — it simply falls
through to AdMob, which looks identical to Ad Manager having no demand. If Ad Manager never
seems to fill, this is the first thing to check.
The app ID is the same for both networks and is already compiled in (see mobile_app_id /
tv_app_id below): AdMob and Ad Manager share one app record when the accounts are linked.
A brand-new GAM unit returns no fill for a few hours up to ~24h after creation. Not a bug.
Wait it out before concluding anything.
Every adx.test below already holds the matching demo path, so a debug build walks the real GAM
code path — request, fill, show — without touching your Ad Manager account:
rewarded .......... /21775744923/example/rewarded
interstitial ...... /21775744923/example/interstitial
adaptive banner ... /21775744923/example/fixed-size-banner
app open .......... /21775744923/example/app-open
Those paths belong to Google's demo network, 21775744923, not to yours — which is exactly why
the network-code check is applied to live and never to test: a test value is used as written,
so the demo paths keep working if this file is ever copied to another account. AdMob's test
unit still sits behind it in the priority list, so a slot whose adx test path cannot fill falls
back rather than going blank.
mobile_app_id / tv_app_id are DOCUMENTATION and are already compiled into the app. The app
never reads an app ID from a remote file: initialisation happens before this file can be
fetched, and a remote switch for the app identity would be a way to break every install at
once. Unit IDs are validated against a compiled publisher / network check, never against this
file — a document checked against itself is not checked. Neither ID is a secret: both ship in
plain text inside every APK. Never put anything that authenticates in this file (AdMob API or
OAuth credentials, service accounts, keys).
reward_gates: comma list from movies,shows,search,record,addplaylist,theme. Empty = no gate is
active even when unlock_rew is served, so every feature stays free.
reward_unlock_hours: clamped to 1-720 in code. 0, negative, or unparseable falls back to 6 — an
unclamped 0 would re-lock the feature the instant the ad finished. mobile and tv hold this
value independently and are both 1 hour today.
Nothing here can lock a user out: if no rewarded ad can be served by ANY source in the
priority list, the gate opens and the feature is free. Never a paywall.
TV: the TV app serves the rewarded ad and nothing else. Its host returns null for attachBanner
and passes interstitials straight through, so a banner or interstitial slot added to tv.slots
would be parsed and then ignored. Google's own GMA Next-Gen SDK page states that the SDK 'does
not support Android TV', which is why tv.slots.unlock_rew.adx.enabled is FALSE by default: TV
keeps serving the AdMob rewarded unit it uses today, with no behaviour change. Its GAM path and
its GAM demo path are both filled in below, so flipping that one key — no release, no other
edit — is the whole change if Ad Manager is ever seen filling on a real box.
SLOT KEY vs name — two naming systems, joined only by the unit ID:
the slot KEY (player_fullscreen_banner) is what the app's code reads. Renaming it is a code
change, so it never changes.
name (INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYER_FULLSCREEN) is only the label typed into the console. NO code reads
it. Rename it in the console whenever you like — the app cannot tell. It sits here so this
file alone tells you which console unit's ID belongs in which live field.
format = what to pick at the console's 'Ad format' step, and fixed when the unit is created: a
unit made as a Banner can never serve a rewarded request. phase and publisher are rollout
documentation, same as the app IDs.
_note = which screens the slot actually serves, so this file answers that without reading code.
THIS FILE HOLDS EXACTLY WHAT THE APP ASKS FOR — 9 mobile keys, 1 TV key, nothing else. The 9
mobile keys are the same 9 in MobileAdMobHost.slotFallbacks, one for one. Adding a key the code
does not read does nothing: it is parsed, stored and never looked up. A new placement is always
code first, then a key here — never a key here in the hope it turns on.
TWO REWARDED UNITS, NOT ONE. mobile.slots.unlock_rew and tv.slots.unlock_rew are different
inventory under different AdMob apps, and their Ad Manager units belong to different GAM
inventory again. Pasting the same unit into both would mis-attribute every impression in the
account. The demo units are legitimately the same string in both — only the live units differ.
PUBLISHING: edit this file in the project folder, then copy it to the inoxtv-config repo
unchanged. Do not edit the hosted copy directly, and do not write this file from inside
inoxtv-config — the project copy is the one that gets reviewed and committed.

unlock_rew.name: INX_MOB_REW_UNLOCK
unlock_rew._note: The feature gates listed in reward_gates. Never a paywall: if neither source can serve it the gate opens rather than locking the user out. The only slot where a missing ad is visible to the user as something other than a missing ad.

app_open.name: INX_MOB_APPOPEN_RESUME
app_open._note: Shown on a real return to the foreground only. Never on first launch, never on rotation, never on internal navigation, and never over a return the app itself asked for (external player, file picker, consent form, store).

fullscreen_exit_int.name: INX_MOB_INT_FULLSCREEN_EXIT
fullscreen_exit_int._note: Leaving a fullscreen player — live TV, movies, shows. The player exits first and the ad opens over the screen behind it, so the user is never held in fullscreen waiting on an ad. max_per_session 0 or missing means never.

section_switch_int.name: INX_MOB_INT_SECTION_SWITCH
section_switch_int._note: IMPLEMENTED but switched off. Flip enabled to true to start showing it, no release needed. Fires only on a real sidebar section change, never on re-selecting the section already open.

livetv_browse_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_LIVETV_BROWSE
livetv_browse_banner._note: The live-TV BROWSE band only, at 100 dp: the channel list, the guide and the small preview player. Live TV in FULLSCREEN is NOT this unit — it is player_fullscreen_banner, at 50 dp. They are still the same physical view (ad_band_live_tv), and FullscreenModeBinder rebinds it from one slot to the other on every fullscreen toggle, which is why toggling costs one ad request. Consequence for reading this file: impressions here are browse impressions only.

catalog_browse_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_CATALOG_BROWSE
catalog_browse_banner._note: Movies, Shows, Recordings and My List browse bands.

player_fullscreen_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYER_FULLSCREEN
player_fullscreen_banner._note: Every band drawn over a video, at 50 dp: live TV in fullscreen (which arrives here when the mode toggles — see livetv_browse_banner), the Movies and Shows fullscreen players, and the recording player. Highest-volume placement in the app, and the only one that shares a surface with the picture.

onboarding_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_ONBOARDING
onboarding_banner._note: The whole playlist-setup flow — welcome home, the type picker, and the M3U, Xtream, Stalker and EPG form pages. Six screens on one unit on purpose: they are the lowest-volume placements in the app and the user sees exactly one at a time, so splitting them would divide the impressions that teach the network what this inventory is worth. The delete-confirm page carries no band and never will, because a banner beside a destructive button is a mis-tap trap.

playlist_processing_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYLIST_PROCESSING
playlist_processing_banner._note: The playlist-processing screen — the longest-dwell screen in the app, because importing a large M3U or Xtream playlist takes minutes. On its own unit rather than sharing onboarding_banner's because the network prices a unit on the behaviour it sees, and mixing a several-minute screen in with six screens the user passes through in seconds would teach it the wrong thing about both.

unlock_rew.name: INX_TV_REW_UNLOCK
unlock_rew._note: The ONLY ad the TV app serves, by design. TV has no banner, no app-open and no interstitial, so a slot added here in those formats would be parsed and then ignored. adx.enabled is false because Google documents the Next-Gen SDK as not supporting Android TV — TV stays on the AdMob unit it serves today. Its Ad Manager path and demo path are filled in anyway, so flipping this one key is the whole change if a real box is seen filling from Ad Manager.
